_comment: Static copy carried over verbatim from docs/prototype/streakforge_data.json. Numbers are NOT stored here; they come from data/processed/*.csv.

kpi_01.name: Overall Churn Rate
kpi_01.defn: Share of members whose latest billing cycle ended more than 30 days before the pipeline as-of date (2026-08-14).
kpi_01.note: Read with kpi_15. The pipeline date sits 313 days past the last real event, so this figure is inflated by missing data, not only by behaviour.

kpi_02.name: Overall Retention Rate
kpi_02.note: The mirror of kpi_01, so it carries the same as-of caveat.

kpi_03.name: Active Members
kpi_03.defn: Members not classified as churned as of the pipeline as-of date.
kpi_03.note: This is the population the composite risk score runs on: Low 487, Moderate 403, Elevated 109, High 12.

kpi_04.name: 7-Day Activation Rate
kpi_04.defn: Share of members who log any gym or app event within 7 days of their join date.
kpi_04.note: The largest single drop in the funnel: 81.2% of members never engage in week one.

kpi_05.name: Renewal Follow-Through Rate
kpi_05.defn: Of members who ever subscribed, the share who renewed at least once more.
kpi_05.note: Healthy next to activation. Renewal is not where the platform leaks.

kpi_06.name: Median Revenue per Member
kpi_06.defn: Median total rupees paid per member. Median is preferred because spend is heavily right-skewed.
kpi_06.note: Quote this one when you need a typical member.

kpi_07.name: Mean Revenue per Member
kpi_07.defn: Mean total rupees paid per member, reported next to the median to show the skew.
kpi_07.note: Roughly double the median: a few large payers pull the mean up.

kpi_08.name: Discount Utilisation Rate
kpi_08.defn: Share of distinct renewal records with a discount applied.

kpi_09.name: Corporate Tie-Up Mix
kpi_09.defn: Share of distinct renewal records under a corporate tie-up plan.

kpi_10.name: Median Plan-to-Engagement Ratio
kpi_10.defn: Median rupees paid per logged gym session. Surfaces members who are paying but not showing up.
kpi_10.note: The twelve flagged members sit at 48,000 to 102,000 on this measure.

kpi_11.name: Avg Weekly Session Rate
kpi_11.defn: Mean of each member's rolling 4-week sessions per week.

kpi_12.name: Avg Session Consistency Score
kpi_12.defn: Mean coefficient of variation of the gaps between sessions. Lower means more regular attendance.
kpi_12.note: The name is misleading: a lower score is better.

kpi_13.name: Avg Streak Length
kpi_13.defn: Mean of each member's average streak length.

kpi_14.name: Streak-Break Recovery Rate
kpi_14.defn: Share of finished streaks followed by a gym check-in within 14 days (streak grain).
kpi_14.note: Over all finished streaks in the raw table the figure is 10.3%. The two differ because of the denominator.

kpi_15.name: Churn Rate (data-realistic as-of)
kpi_15.defn: The same churn logic anchored at the last real event in the data, 2025-10-05.
kpi_15.note: Treat this as the operationally meaningful number and always show it beside kpi_01.

insights.title: Churn looks catastrophic at 94%, but much of it is a measurement artefact
insights.story: The pipeline's fixed as-of date (2026-08-14) sits well past the dataset's actual last event (2025-10-05), so almost every member reads as churned. Re-anchoring to a data-realistic date drops churn to 84.0%. That is still high, but the 94.0% headline should never be quoted to leadership without this context.
insights.evidence: kpi_01 against kpi_15 in kpi_summary.csv; the PR9 and PR11 as-of decision.
insights.impact: High. Wrong framing risks over-reacting, for example with panic win-back spend, to a partly artefactual number.
insights.action: Report churn with both figures side by side. Treat kpi_15 as the operationally meaningful number.

insights.title: Activation, not renewal, is where the platform loses members
insights.story: Only 18.8% of members log any activity within 7 days of joining. That is an 81.2% drop at a single stage and the largest of any funnel step. No acquisition channel or demographic segment explains it: every Cramér's V is below 0.1.
insights.impact: High. This is the single highest-leverage retention lever found in the dataset.
insights.action: Prioritise onboarding experiments on UX and timing over channel-targeted acquisition spend.

insights.title: Activation is quietly improving, so the funnel is not getting worse
insights.story: Monthly cohort activation rose from about 14.6% in late 2024 to about 36.6% in September 2025. It is the most encouraging non-obvious finding in the dataset and the opposite of what the 81.2% headline drop-off implies in isolation.
insights.impact: Medium. It reframes the story from a broken funnel to an improving one worth investing in.
insights.action: Investigate what changed operationally in early 2025 and double down on it.

insights.title: Churn and activation are platform-wide problems, not a branch-operations issue
insights.story: None of the 40 branches is a statistical churn-rate outlier, and none combines a churn anomaly with bottom-quartile activation. That rules out a few bad branches as the root cause.
insights.evidence: branch_risk_summary.csv (0 of 40 flagged); PR11 section 11.2.2 and PR12 section 12.1(c).
insights.impact: Medium. It redirects the investigation away from branch staffing and operations, toward product and onboarding.
insights.action: Do not fund a branch-level operational audit as a churn fix. Focus centrally on onboarding.

insights.title: A small, well-defined 'paid once, never engaged' cohort is ready for outreach
insights.story: Twelve currently-active members trigger nearly every composite risk signal. Most are single-event members paying 48,000 to 102,000 rupees per logged session. It is a short, actionable list rather than a diffuse population-wide signal.
insights.impact: Medium. The volume is small, but the win-back value per member is high and the targeting cost is low.
insights.action: Reach out directly, by call or PT trial offer, to the 12 flagged members within the next billing cycle.
